text:
maya: FYI customer StitchPay (CS-4983) says their canary rollout health chart has been stuck on 'in progress' for ~45m. UI shows inflight, no success/fail. They say API returns 200 for status queries but chart never transitions. This is blocking auto-promote and alerts. Can we triage?

isaac: Do we have any UI logs or the rollout id? Any errors from status-sync?

maya: Rollout id: r-9a7c4b. Screenshot pasted to ticket. Quick paste of the API response I got:
```
GET /api/v1/rollouts/r-9a7c4b/status
200 OK
{
  "id": "r-9a7c4b",
  "status": "IN_PROGRESS",
  "last_update": null,
  "steps": [{"step": "canary-check", "result": null}]
}
```

devon: I see a spike in status-sync worker errors around 10:12 UTC. From logs: 
```
2026-03-15T10:12:08Z status-sync consumer=5 shard=2 ERROR syncer: failed to fetch model_status for r-*: 504 gateway timeout
2026-03-15T10:12:09Z status-sync consumer=5 shard=2 ERROR syncer: retrying (attempt 3)
2026-03-15T10:12:10Z status-sync consumer=5 shard=2 WARN queue length=10342
```

lee: That queue length matches the monitoring alert — kafka topic `rollout-status` had sustained backlog. Connection pool changes deployed earlier could have reduced concurrency to model-query service; consumers timed out and left rollouts IN_PROGRESS.

isaac: Short-term workaround: there's an admin force-sync endpoint we can use to re-evaluate rollout state. Example command: 
```
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  "https://console.redwood.ai/admin/rollouts/force-sync?ids=r-9a7c4b"
```
Also restarting one status-sync consumer tends to drain the backlog.

maya: I ran the force-sync for r-9a7c4b and it moved to DONE within ~30s. Customer confirmed the chart updated and alerts re-evaluated. Still multiple other rollouts remain stuck across a few accounts.

devon: I'll run a targeted backfill to rehydrate missing status events from event-sink into the analytics pipeline for affected rollouts. Planning a short job now — will annotate affected customers.

sophia: Thanks — resolved for that rollout. We rely on canary metrics to auto-promote; what's the ETA for a permanent fix so this doesn't happen again?

lee: Investigating root cause. Preliminary plan: revert the pool change that reduced model-query concurrency and deploy a status-sync patch with a circuit-breaker + exponential backoff. ETA: patch tomorrow morning PST, plus validation.

oncall-bot: INCIDENT CREATED: INC-2026-213 - Canary status-sync degradation (Sev 2). Pager duty alerted.

maya: Assigning ENG-RUNTIME and ENG-PLATFORM to own the hotfix and postmortem. I'll update CS-4983 and notify affected accounts with the temporary workaround (force-sync + restart).

devon: I'll document the runbook (force-sync, restart consumer, run backfill) and add it to ops playbook. :thumbsup:

isaac: Added a quick Grafana dashboard link to the ticket (consumer lag, queue size, 5xx rates). Leaving a pinned note for on-call.

maya: thanks everyone, I'll follow up with the customer once we have a timeline and postmortem.
